Hi everyone!
@L1kwair bisected an issue (thanks!) to commit #0fc082e, the changes here increase times up to 60ms and tank performance as @wheatear-dev mentioned,

this issue also looks to be related to: #105248 and #108435 (partly fixed in: #108530).
the main regression most likely comes from #90644, which includes #0fc082e.

I looked into it and parts of it have to do with this setting:

```xml
<member name="debug_fill" type="bool" setter="set_enable_debug_fill" getter="get_enable_debug_fill" default="true">
			If [code]true[/code], when the shape is displayed, it will show a solid fill color in addition to its wireframe.
</member>
```

`debug_fill`, which is true by default, I tested by setting it to false and, for me this improves performance, while not seeing much difference (or any) visually.

I think a partial fix would be to set `debug_fill` default to false, and let users opt-in if needed, but there might be additional regressions from somewhere which would need taking care of to fully fix (see #105248)

Who would've though #90644 would cause so many problems lol

debug_fill set to false by default makes sense at this point as a first change, but why would we want to have users opt-in, especially if there's not much difference visually and only a massive performance hit?

And do you think that updating debug_fill should suffice for this issue? The performance fix being worked on in #105248 may resolve this issue indirectly since it seems to be the root cause.

looking into the matter further and will In Sha ALLAH try to propose a proper solution.

Just reading the code, I'm still a little new to the code but I notice that the layer mask isolates gizmos to the editor view only. It seems like even though Gizmos are isolated, they are still handled in the render pipeline as MATERIAL with Meshes. I think what is happening is each surface is getting added to the secondary render list. Draw call inflation would occur because each surface in MATERIAL would go to secondary pass. All the surfaces will be rendered even if the object is editor only. Combined with the Gizmos always being visible, that allows for the potential for duplicate draws.

I was looking at maybe adding something to identify Gizmos in the pipeline, possibly in the RenderGeometryInstance? Could a senior maintainer advise if that approach makes sense, or if there’s a better way to handle editor-only objects in the pipeline?

Sorry for the multiple comments, after going through the code base I think the best idea is to assign a GeometryInstanceSurfaceDataCache enum flag for Gizmo objects so that they don't end up going through multiple secondary passes. Right now there is no differentiation for object type (normal mesh vs Gizmo). Perhaps in EditorNode3DGizmo::Instance::create_instance, then the flag would  be checked in _fill_render_list to skip Gizmo surfaces in MATERIAL/SHADOW passes, avoiding unnecessary draw calls. If that sounds good to maintainers I'm down to give it a shot.

I did some research again and I don't think there actually is anything to fix here. Before PR #95640, the _fill_instance_data call in _render_scene (the one that passes the alpha list) didn't include render_info. Which if I understand it correctly, is just a counter for how many alpha draw calls will be made that frame. But the gizmos were still being rendered, even though they should be incrementing that count. After the PR, the count was now being passed, including all of the gizmos. So while it seems like the performance is degraded and the count is indicating what seems to be many more draw calls, it's really just book-keeping.

Bottom line, I think the issue should be closed.

Hey, I'm new, was reading through this issue out of curiosity.

tl;dr - I don't think this should be closed yet. I'd suggest caching the constructed debug ArrayMesh that's built by the subclasses of `Shape3D` (introduced in the commit identified from the bisect search).

I'm reading through the current code on the master branch, and I'd expect the editor to be spending a good chunk of time rebuilding the debug ArrayMesh for collision shapes in the scene from the repro project (lots of objects with collision in view in the repro gifs), which would could contribute significantly to a CPU usage spike when they're all in view.

Digging in a bit, [CollisionShape3DGizmoPlugin::redraw](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/master/editor/scene/3d/gizmos/physics/collision_shape_3d_gizmo_plugin.cpp#L304) calls out to `Shape3D::get_debug_arraymesh_faces`, which (in each of `Shape3D`'s implementing classes, eg [HeightMapShape3D](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/master/scene/resources/3d/height_map_shape_3d.cpp#L89)), now holds the the ArrayMesh construction code that is included in the commit from the bisect search (which is to say, it appears to rebuild the debug ArrayMesh faces on every redraw, which for the performance hit, I'm guessing is every frame)

This would be improved by generating+caching the ArrayMesh and rebuilding it only when the collision shape is updated. Incidentally, `Shape3D` already has a `debug_mesh_cache` member it uses to cache a different mesh, so assuming however that's used isn't seeing any stale-cache issues with the debug mesh, that could be a helpful reference for implementing the change.

In the spirit of clear communication, I'm not planning to work on this at the moment..

I'd like to investigate this. Since it's confirmed as a regression between v4.3-stable and v4.4-stable, I'll start by bisecting the editor/gizmo rendering commits between those versions using the linked minimal repro project to narrow down which change introduced the draw-call blowup. Will report back with findings before proposing a fix, since a regression like this in the rendering server could have a few different causes.

> Since it's confirmed as a regression between v4.3-stable and v4.4-stable, I'll start by bisecting the editor/gizmo rendering commits between those versions using the linked minimal repro project to narrow down which change introduced the draw-call blowup.

The issue has already been bisected [above](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/issues/103676#issuecomment-3362010378).

I just ran through bobjegers comment and confirmed on my own machine that I see something like a 40-60% improvement in FPS with `get_debug_arraymesh_faces` cut out of the `CollisionShape3DGizmoPlugin::redraw` method. Going to pick this up and see if I can't implement caching here.

I implemented a naive cache to test, and logged on any miss to ensure that the cached ArrayMesh was actually being used, and it resulted in very little real change to performance. The FPS with the initially placed camera in the editor went from about 128 to 130. This was with no misses (outside of the initial logs before any generation).

In retrospect, I could have narrowed further by simply letting that code run and removing the call to `add_mesh`. Removing that line results in the expected frame rate gain.
